subject: Demo: prefetch slowdown causing generation timeouts
messages:
From: Caitlin Morgan <caitlin@atlashealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: atlas-demo+ops@atlashealth.com
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Demo: prefetch slowdown causing generation timeouts

Hi Hannah —

Quick note from the demo earlier today. During the second scenario the model went from ~120ms/token to bursts of 1.5–3s/token and a handful of requests timed out entirely. We captured the session and exported logs (attached). The demo was using the prefix-based prefetch mode you recommended in the onboarding docs.

The slowdown started at approx 10:43 PDT and affected 3 of 12 calls in that demo window; the rest were fine. I’ve attached the logs and a brief repro script. Can you help triage? This is blocking our next internal signoff.

What we saw (high level):
- Streaming stalled mid-sequence (client saw partial tokens then a long pause)
- Server returned 502/timeout for two attempts
- No client-side network drops observed

Attaching: atlas_degradation_logs_20270226.zip (contains server logs, client capture, and a short Node repro)

Thanks,
Caitlin Morgan
Technical Program Manager, AtlasHealth

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Caitlin Morgan <caitlin@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 17:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Demo: prefetch slowdown causing generation timeouts

Caitlin — thanks for the replay and logs. Looping in Sean (sales-eng) and Platform/Runtime (Logan + Dev) to triage.

High-level ask for internal: can we confirm whether this looks like a prefetch/KV-cache eviction issue vs. routing/burst autoscale? Customer used the hosted API with prefetch enabled and standard routing. They’re in the us-west region.

Customer-facing plan: we want a short canary patch (route them to a variant with prefetch disabled + enable extended timeouts) while we investigate the root cause. If platform can do that today we’ll coordinate with Atlas for a quick recon and demo retest.

Attachments: atlas_degradation_logs_20270226.zip (forwarded)

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 09:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Demo: prefetch slowdown causing generation timeouts

Quick initial triage after a first pass on the logs:
- Evidence of repeated KV cache miss/eviction for the same session ID (see server.log lines: kvcache.evicted session=41f7...). That would cause the runtime to rehydrate prefix state and produce pauses as it fetches context back into GPU memory.
- I also see a handful of requests routed to a lower-priority pool during a short autoscaler window (autoscale events around 10:42–10:45 PDT). There’s a correlation but not conclusive causation yet.

Action items I need from Atlas/Hannah:
1) The exact request ids with timestamps for the stalled calls (we have a few candidates but need confirmation) — put into sample_request_ids.txt if you can.
2) If possible, run the small repro with the environment variable REDWOOD_TRACE=1 and upload the trace link (we can parse it directly).

Temporary mitigation we can do immediately:
- Route the Atlas account to a variant with prefetch disabled and bump request-level timeouts to 90s. That will avoid KV cache rehydrate stalls at the expense of higher per-token CPU work.

I’ve uploaded the initial parsing to the internal trace: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/trace-7b9f3 — contains the relevant kvcache traces and autoscale events.

Dev Patel
Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 10:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Demo: prefetch slowdown causing generation timeouts

Thanks Dev — that aligns with what I’m seeing in the routing layer. Two quick notes from Platform:

1) We can enact the workaround Logan proposed (route to prefetch-disabled variant + timeout bump) via Console and roll it to Atlas as a canary in ~15 minutes. I’ll coordinate the canary rollout window and health checks.

2) Product ask / roadmap question for Neha: we should evaluate adding an "api_prefetch_enabled" flag surfaced at the account-level API and SDK config (vs. only being an internal runtime knob). It would let Sales/CS toggle prefetch for a customer without internal platform changes. This is currently a platform-only control. Neha — can we discuss whether this fits in the next quarter's roadmap or if there’s an interim support-side toggle we can expose?

Recommendation: short-term mitigation + post-mortem. Long-term: either make prefetch toggleable via API or harden kvcache eviction heuristics for session hotness.

Logan Wright
Director, Platform Engineering, Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.ai

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Caitlin Morgan <caitlin@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 11:00:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Demo: prefetch slowdown causing generation timeouts

Caitlin — thank you for the fast repro and logs. Plan for the next 24 hours:
- Immediate canary: we will route your account to a variant with prefetch disabled and bump timeouts to 90s. Expect the change within 30 minutes. We’ll monitor the next demo and confirm whether stalls persist.
- Dev/Platform will continue root-cause triage (Dev has asked for request ids and a REDWOOD_TRACE output; I’ll upload sample_request_ids.txt shortly).
- Product ask: We’ll circle back about a permanent toggle; Neha is cc’d.

Can everyone join a quick 20-minute call at 13:00 PDT today to sync on the mitigation and required telemetry? Caitlin — does that work for you?

Thanks — we’ll follow up with the canary status and a short summary post-check.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
